rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When a messenger prays this way, God immediately delivers His verdict and punishment breaks the disbelievers.
rows.anchor: When a messenger prays with these words, God’s verdict is immediately delivered and divine punishment breaks the backs of these disbelievers.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses describe the afterlife punishment awaiting the rebellious.
rows.anchor: This verse describes the punishment these rebellious people will face in the hereafter.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the afterlife, disbelieving leaders and followers curse one another, and Satan disowns his followers.
rows.anchor: Leaders will curse their followers and the followers will curse their leaders. Even Satan will announce his acquittal from his followers.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers will dwell comfortably in Paradise and exchange greetings.
rows.anchor: On the other hand, the believers will be lodged comfortably in Paradise and will exchange greetings.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The addressed disbelievers are polytheists; polytheism is disbelief, and only monotheistic belief is acceptable.
rows.anchor: The disbelievers here refer to the polytheists who are addressed here. Polytheism is in fact disbelief.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Associating others with God in His being, attributes, or rights is unacceptable and amounts to denying Him.
rows.anchor: are associated with Him in His being, attributes and rights, then this belief is not acceptable.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ashes image concerns the polytheists’ deeds on Judgement Day, deeds they had regarded as virtuous.
rows.anchor: These deeds obviously will be ones that they had done considering them to be virtuous.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deviation is an error from which they cannot return; a profound parallel appears in the cited verses.
rows.anchor: Readers may look up verse 3 of this sūrah. Another very profound example of such people is mentioned in verse 39 of Sūrah al-Nūr.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh are threatened: the purposeful world conflicts with their way of life, and God can easily replace them with a new creation.
rows.anchor: This world has been created with a purpose while their life is against this purpose.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although merciful, God also upholds justice; destroying those who have dismantled justice and fairness is no burden to Him.
rows.anchor: destroy such people who themselves have destroyed the system of justice and fairness

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Barūz means emerging from behind a barrier; the word evokes idolaters leaving their deities, once used as shields, and standing before God without support.
rows.anchor: The actual meaning of the word ﺑـﺮوزis to come out from behind a barrier or shield.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan distinguishes God’s true promise from his own broken promises, denies coercive power, and disowns the disbelievers who followed his invitation.
rows.anchor: God’s promise as true whereas the promises he made were false.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers greet each other with peace because they counseled one another toward the right path and thus reached Paradise; this contrasts with the disbelievers’ mutual curses.
rows.anchor: They will greet one another with peace because they counseled one another in the right direction.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coming parables contrast polytheistic and monotheistic belief: polytheism lacks grounding in human reason, nature, or God, so deeds built on it vanish.
rows.anchor: polytheism has no basis – neither in human intellect and nature nor with God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Monotheism is grounded in human intellect, nature, and divine guidance; it is firmly rooted and brings adherents success in both worlds.
rows.anchor: it is deeply routed in the earth and its branches are vastly spread in the sky.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not compel people to choose the right path; He wants them to choose it freely.
rows.anchor: He wants people to choose the right path from their own will.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The harmony of nature’s conflicting elements indicates monotheism: one powerful will governs the universe, with no other deity sharing in it.
rows.anchor: The harmony in conflicting elements of nature in this universe bears evidence to the belief of monotheism.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those relying on other deities without fearing the Hereafter will face the consequences of their arrogance.
rows.anchor: people who rely on other deities and have no fear of the hereafter

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arrogant leaders who disillusion people about the Qur’an will bear their own misguidance and a share of others’ because they caused it; the righteous fare well.
rows.anchor: will bear the burden of their deviance as well as a part of others because they were responsible for them going astray.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūrah cites and refutes idolaters’ arguments against the Qur’an and in support of their baseless views.
rows.anchor: Some of the arguments the idolaters proffered to oppose the Qur’ ān and support their baseless views are cited and refuted.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those enduring hardship for the truth are encouraged, while the polytheists are warned against arrogance.
rows.anchor: Those who were putting up with hardships from the idolaters merely for the cause of truth are encouraged

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arguments establish God’s control over everything: if He seizes the idolaters, no one can save them.
rows.anchor: everything is in God’s control. If He seizes them, no one can save them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives respite because each event has an appointed time; when it arrives, it cannot be delayed or advanced.
rows.anchor: if God has given them respite, it is because there is time fixed for every event.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is assured that earlier messengers faced the same opposition; his duty is to convey the truth conclusively, not convert people.
rows.anchor: His task is not to convert people into believers; he is only required to conclusively communicate the truth to them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Recounting God’s favors rebukes the idolaters for attributing them elsewhere; the Prophet need only communicate truth to those feigning ignorance.
rows.anchor: By recounting certain favours of God before the idolaters, they are rebuked

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent messengers to every community to convey the truth and testify on Judgement Day; Muhammad has the same role for his community, with a revealed Book for this purpose.
rows.anchor: God has sent messengers to every community to convey the truth to it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Jews broke their covenant out of jealousy, like a woman undoing her spun thread; they must not trade it for worldly wealth or use oaths to turn people from truth.
rows.anchor: They are like an old women who spins her thread and then shreds it into bits.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who persevere in truth despite opposition are promised the best reward in this world and the next.
rows.anchor: People who persevere on the truth in spite of opposition from their rivals are promised best reward both in this world and in the next.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūrah answers objections raised to create doubts about the Qur’an and the Prophet among the masses.
rows.anchor: objections which people were raising to create doubts in the minds of the masses against the Qur’ān and the Prophet (sws) are answered.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Persecuted Muslims are reassured, those who abandon Islam under hardship are warned, and migration for truth and its reward are indicated.
rows.anchor: Assurance is sounded to Muslims who were suffering at the hands of the enemies of the truth

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ruined city warns Quraysh to change; they must consume what God permits rather than invent prohibitions from superstition or desire.
rows.anchor: An example of a city is cited in order to warn the Quraysh

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Jews arrogantly attributed their own prohibitions to Abraham, though Abraham was neither Jew, Christian, nor idolater; his distinct religion is the Prophet’s model, and Sabbath observance belonged to Jews.
rows.anchor: Abraham (sws) was neither a Jew, nor a Christian nor an Idolater.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet and Muslims should invite wisely, persevere through God-connection, and trust that God accompanies His righteous servants despite opponents’ conspiracies.
rows.anchor: The means of acquiring this perseverance is God-connection.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s gratitude distinguished him from idolaters who credited idols for God’s favors; because of that gratitude, God chose and guided him.
rows.anchor: It was because of this grateful attitude of theirs that God chose him to be a prophet and guided him to a straight path.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham received goodness in this world, including a position of authority, and will have a high rank among the righteous in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: Abraham (sws) was granted a position of authority so that he virtually became a ruler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jews, Christians, and idolaters who claim Abraham’s religion are liars, while the Prophet is directed to follow Abraham’s way.
rows.anchor: all these Jews, Christians and Idolaters who claim to be followers of Abraham’s (sws) religion are absolute liars.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrah al-Isrāʾ is al-Naḥl’s counterpart: they share a theme, with the later sūrah explaining in detail what the earlier presented concisely.
rows.anchor: This sūrah is the counterpart of S ūrah al-Naḥl, the previous sūrah.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Israelites’ chosen-people claim is self-deception; their history shows rebellion brought punishment, while repentance and reform made them worthy of mercy, and they must follow this prophet’s Torah-aligned call.
rows.anchor: Their own history bears witness that whenever they rebelled against God, they were severely punished.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ascension signals that the Kaaba and Aqsa custodianships were taken from their corrupt custodians for embezzling the trust and assigned to the unlettered Prophet.
rows.anchor: God has now decided to entrust their custodianship to this unlettered prophet.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an’s detailed natural path matches the Torah’s Ten Commandments: human nature and ancient revelation agree, and rebels among Quraysh or Israel will be punished.
rows.anchor: human nature and ancient divine teachings are in harmony with one another.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Migration, mentioned only briefly in al-Naḥl, is clearly commanded in this sūrah; the directions indicate that it is near.
rows.anchor: It is evident from the way in which these directions are given that its time is near.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ascension signifies that custodianship of the Kaaba and Aqsa was removed from those who embezzled it and handed to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: Their custodianship has been handed over to the Prophet (sws).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Israelites’ claim to exclusive religious leadership is rejected: prophets foretold two rebellions and punishments, borne out by Chaldean and Roman conquests; reform brought release, and they must accept the unlettered Prophet’s invitation or face punishment again.
rows.anchor: Thus their history bears witness that first they were beaten up at the hands of the Chaldeans and then by the Romans.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an invites Quraysh and Israelites to the natural path taught by earlier prophets and scriptures, promising good to accepters and destruction to rejecters; they ignore signs and demand miracles.
rows.anchor: Both the Idolaters of the Quraysh and the Israelites are invited to profess faith in the Qur’ ān.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No soul carries another’s burden, and God’s established practice is to warn and admonish people before punishment; these audiences have now been fully warned.
rows.anchor: It is God’s way that He does not punish people without warning and admonishing them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight-path details correspond to the prior sūrah’s verse 90, the Torah’s Ten Commandments, and human nature; Abraham, Moses, and Jesus all taught them.
rows.anchor: the ten commandments of the Torah and these teachings of the Qur’ ān are in complete harmony

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh’s aversion stems from refusing monotheism and the Hereafter; they flee and mock the recitation, although both beliefs are plainly reasoned.
rows.anchor: The real reason for the aversion of the Idolaters of the Quraysh is alluded to: they do not want to profess faith in monotheism and belief in the Hereafter.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Monotheism and belief in the Hereafter are reasoned so clearly that no sane person can reject them.
rows.anchor: both these beliefs have been reasoned out so clearly that no sane person can reject them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: During heated preaching the Prophet should restrain companions from provoking rivals lest Satan exploit it; his duty is preaching, while God grants or withholds the urge to believe.
rows.anchor: Forcibly making people accept Islam is not his duty.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave each prophet superiority in some respect, so claims of absolute superiority should be avoided lest they become a trial.
rows.anchor: God has made all his prophets superior to others in some aspect or the other.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the parenthetical address to the Prophet, the monotheism discussion resumes: angels seek God’s nearness and fear His punishment, so cannot be His associates.
rows.anchor: they themselves continuously strive for the nearness of God and to please Him and at all times are in awe of His punishment

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demand that God’s punishment be shown is answered by explaining His established practice regarding punishment.
rows.anchor: The demand of the Prophet’s enemies that they be shown the torment of God is answered

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelievers became arrogant and ungrateful for God’s favors, following Satan, whose thought about them was fulfilled.
rows.anchor: instead of being grateful to God on His favours, they took to disbelief and because arrogant.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A parable portrays arrogance after receiving favors and contrasts those who live with open eyes with those who wander blind.
rows.anchor: A parable is cited that depicts the arrogance of a person once he is blessed with favours.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet must continue preaching despite opposition; if Quraysh expel him, they will not remain long, in keeping with God’s practice concerning prophetic migration.
rows.anchor: if the Quraysh turn him out from this land, then they too will not be able to reside in it for long.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is urged to persevere through prayer and supplication as migration nears, with glad tidings that truth will prevail.
rows.anchor: It is indicated that the time of migration is near.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is a cure and mercy that no human or jinn could reproduce; an objection about revelation and Gabriel is answered.
rows.anchor: If all of mankind and jinnkind together try to author such a Book, they would not be able to.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh’s miracle demands are answered, and the arrogant are reminded that prophethood is God’s favor, not a privilege they can claim as sole owners of His treasures.
rows.anchor: they are not the sole owners of God’s treasures and thus have no right to think that they are the sole recipients of propethood.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage recalls Moses’ nine miracles and alludes to Pharaoh’s fate for persisting in rebellion despite seeing them.
rows.anchor: The nine miracles worked by Moses (sws) are referred to.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is wholly true; messengers warn and give glad tidings, and gradual revelation suits its teaching, while the Prophet should leave wretched rejecters to themselves.
rows.anchor: If the Qur’ ān is being revealed gradually, then it is because this is the requisite of its teaching.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only those with knowledge’s inner light believe; Allah and Rahman are names of God, and worship should be moderate with continued praise and glorification.
rows.anchor: All āh and Raḥmān are God’s names.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The analysis shows the sūrah as a whole organized around one theme.
rows.anchor: A look at this analysis of the sūrah will show the readers how it stands out as a whole under a single theme.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Subḥān absolves God of every blemish; opening discourse with it corrects mistaken ideas about Him, which is why the ascension account begins with the word.
rows.anchor: When a discourse begins with this word, the purpose is to remove any wrong estimation or misconception about God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ascension was meant to correct the Jews’ and idolaters’ grossly wrong conception of God.
rows.anchor: this incident was meant to dispel a grossly incorrect estimation of God in the mind of he Jews and the Idolaters.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Jews and idolaters controlled the two great religious centers but had turned them from their purpose into places of polytheism and idolatry.
rows.anchor: Contrary to the basic objective of these centres, they had made them a den for polytheism and idolatry.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author compares the sites’ corruption with Jesus’ reported denunciation of a den of robbers and describes both as controlled by dishonest, corrupt factions.
rows.anchor: they had done what precisely Jesus (sws) is reported to have said: you have made it a den of robbers (Luke, 19:46).
